gloss: to use as a stepping stone; to exploit for personal advancement

definitions.gloss: to use as a stepping stone; to exploit someone or something for personal advancement
definitions.explanation: To take advantage of a person, position, or experience as a means of advancing one's own career or goals, often with a negative connotation of using others callously.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{人|ひと}を{踏|ふ}み{台|だい}にして{出世|しゅっせ}した。
examples.english: He climbed the ladder by stepping on others.

examples.japanese: この{経験|けいけん}を{踏|ふ}み{台|だい}にして、{次|つぎ}のステップに{進|すす}みたい。
examples.english: I want to use this experience as a stepping stone to move to the next level.

examples.japanese: {仲間|なかま}を{踏|ふ}み{台|だい}にするような{人|ひと}は{信用|しんよう}されない。
examples.english: People who exploit their colleagues as stepping stones are not trusted.

notes:
Literally 'to make into a stepping stool,' this expression uses the concrete image of a {踏|ふ}み{台|だい} (step stool) as a metaphor for using someone or something to advance. When the object is a person, the expression is distinctly negative, implying opportunistic or callous behavior. When the object is an experience or situation, it can be neutral or even positive.

USAGE:
- Negative: {人|ひと}を{踏|ふ}み{台|だい}にする (to use people as stepping stones)
- Neutral/positive: {経験|けいけん}を{踏|ふ}み{台|だい}にする (to use experience as a stepping stone)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人|ひと}を{踏|ふ}み{台|だい}にする: to exploit people for advancement
- {経験|けいけん}を{踏|ふ}み{台|だい}にする: to use experience as a springboard
- {失敗|しっぱい}を{踏|ふ}み{台|だい}にする: to turn failure into a stepping stone

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {足場|あしば}にする: to use as a foothold — similar metaphor but less negative
- {利用|りよう}する: to use; to take advantage of — broader and more neutral
